summary_responses.response: Cloud microservice architectures, while enabling independent scaling and operation, can suffer from overload due to miscoordination among services, causing high-value transactions to be rejected alongside low-value ones. The paper proposes DiffTry (Differential Retries), a simple, lightweight, and stateless mechanism that assigns different retry limits to different priority classes—e.g., allowing premium users more retries than bypassing users—thereby protecting high-priority transactions during overload without requiring overload detection or inter-service coordination. The authors develop an analytical framework covering both single-service and network-wide settings, proving convergence, monotonicity, and (for DAG-based service graphs) uniqueness of their rejection-rate model, which lets practitioners predict and optimize performance. DiffTry also suppresses retry storms caused by excessive low-priority retries and offers resilience against adversarial overload attacks that target high-value traffic with cheap low-priority requests. The mechanism is validated through simulation and a live Kubernetes deployment as a drop-in service-mesh plugin requiring no application code changes, with measured rejection rates closely matching the analytical predictions.

summary_responses.response: The FAA has issued a final airworthiness directive (AD) effective November 18, 2026, requiring corrections to low-clearance conditions in the right wings of certain Bombardier BD-700-2A12 airplanes, prompted by reports of insufficient spacing between fuel line components, hydraulic systems, and other parts. The directive mandates replacing a clip-nut and fuel tube assemblies and inspecting clearance between the hydraulic system and fuel vent tube, with potential on-condition actions including replacing hydraulic support brackets if low clearance is found. The unsafe condition could lead to an ignition source developing in the fuel tank during a lightning strike if left unaddressed. The FAA estimated the cost of compliance at $2,693 per aircraft across approximately 60 U.S.-registered airplanes (roughly $161,580 total), though some costs may be covered under warranty. Despite comments from some individuals requesting an emergency AD or a reopened comment period, the FAA determined that the compliance times and corrective actions specified in the originating Transport Canada AD are adequate and adopted the rule as proposed.

summary_responses.subtopic: Public Administration, Labor Policy & Family Leave
summary_responses.response: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is issuing a direct final rule making technical revisions to its Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) regulations to reflect statutory amendments enacted in January 2021 and December 2023. The rule broadens FMLA eligibility by making virtually all Federal civilian service—including temporary and intermittent employment—and certain honorable active military service qualify toward the 12-month service requirement. The rule also clarifies that annual or sick leave earned under authorities outside of title 5, U.S. Code may be substituted for unpaid FMLA leave, and excludes Veterans Health Administration employees covered by their own leave system from title 5 FMLA coverage. Because paid parental leave (PPL) eligibility depends on meeting FMLA eligibility requirements, these changes also expand who qualifies for PPL. The rule takes effect December 14, 2026, unless significant adverse comments are received by November 16, 2026, in which case OPM will withdraw the affected provisions and issue a proposed rule instead.
